note: Sourced facts for fact cards. Each 'fit' lists what must be visible in a clip for the fact to be about it.

facts.fact: Reanimal launched on February 13, 2026. It came out on PS5, Xbox Series X/S, Nintendo Switch 2 and PC.
facts.quote: PlayStation Blog: "which launches on PS5 Feb 13, 2026" | TheGamer: "At launch, Reanimal is available on plenty of platforms, including PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, Nintendo Switch 2, and PC through Steam."

facts.fact: Reanimal opens with the boy alone in a small boat, following red lights through the dark sea until he hauls a masked figure out of the water.
facts.quote: PlayStation Blog: "I started as The Boy, floating alone in a boat adrift in a sea of darkness." | PlayStation Blog: "A press of R2 drove me towards a single red light bobbing on the horizon." | PlayStation Blog: "Until eventually I stopped to haul a masked figure out of the sea"

facts.fact: When the boy pulls a girl aboard his boat and reaches for the hare mask covering her face, she pins him down and rips at his mask until he kicks her away.
facts.quote: IGN: "At the fourth buoy, the boy stops the boat and pulls aboard a girl. When he reaches for the hare mask covering her face, she pins him to the small outboard's wooden bottom, her hands ripping at his mask until he kicks her away."

facts.fact: The game never tells you the boy and the girl are brother and sister. You pick it up from how they help and comfort each other.
facts.quote: IGN: "The boy and the girl are brother and sister, but this fact is never told to you. You learn it through the way they help each other up, comfort each other when things go wrong."

facts.fact: The girl can clip her lantern to her hip and still carry things, but the boy can only use his lighter when his hands are free.
facts.quote: IGN: "Little distinguishes the boy from the girl, save that she can attach her lantern to her hip while carrying something else. The boy's lighter, on the other hand, is only usable if his hands are free."

facts.fact: Reanimal has no HUD, no meters and no minimap on screen.
facts.quote: IGN: "There is no HUD, no meters, no minimap."

facts.fact: In co-op you cannot choose who plays who. Player one is the boy and player two is the girl.
facts.quote: IGN: "There is no way to select who plays who; it simply works out this way" | TheGamer: "with the first player being the boy and the second player being the girl"

facts.fact: Co-op uses one shared camera in every mode, local and online, with no split-screen. Tarsier did this so both players are scared together.
facts.quote: Xbox Wire: "When you play co-op, both local and online, it's the same camera in all game modes" | Xbox Wire: "There's no split-screen, and that was to enhance this pillar even more."

facts.fact: Playing solo, the AI sister gives you a boost up to high ledges when you press Triangle, and L1 gets her to use things in the world.
facts.quote: PlayStation Blog: "swiftly responding to a press of the Triangle button when we needed to give each other a boost to out-of-reach platforms." | PlayStation Blog: "Alternatively, a tap of L1 gets her to interact with certain elements in the environment."

facts.fact: There are 18 masks hidden around the world, and you can put them on either child to change their look. Masks carry over between playthroughs.
facts.quote: TheGamer: "There are 18 masks hidden around the world of Reanimal for you to find and collect as you go along." | TheGamer: "You can even equip them on the children to change their look, too!" | TheGamer: "Masks are shared across playthroughs and are tied to your account"

facts.fact: Masks are often found in boxes on floors and tables, near a bigger version of whatever the mask shows.
facts.quote: TheGamer: "They'll often appear in boxes on floors and tables, typically near a larger iteration of what the mask represents."

facts.fact: Pre-orders got two exclusive masks, Foxhead and Muttonhead. Tarsier picked them for their bestial look and their predator and prey pairing.
facts.quote: PlayStation Blog: "All pre-orders of Reanimal unlock a pair of exclusive masks" | PlayStation Blog: "The Foxhead and Muttonhead masks resonated especially well because they had that bestial flavour that we were looking for; while their predator/prey characterisations quietly reiterate the game's thematic undercurrents."

facts.fact: Tarsier, the studio making Reanimal's creepy masks, once made hats and costumes for LittleBigPlanet.
facts.quote: PlayStation Blog: "As a studio that cut its teeth making hats and costumes for LittleBigPlanet, it feels strangely appropriate to be back here all these years later talking about the masks of Reanimal." | GamesRadar: "Tarsier worked on LittleBigPlanet and Tearaway from 2008 to 2015"

facts.fact: There are 20 black posters with red art to find. Each one you tear down unlocks concept art in the main menu.
facts.quote: TheGamer: "These black posters with red art are here, there, and everywhere, and every one you take down when you find it unlocks some pretty spooky concept art for Reanimal in the main menu of the game. There are 20 to find, also with an achievement for finding them all."

facts.fact: You can sit down at hidden resting spots, including chairs, cages and even toilets. Sitting in ten of them earns a trophy.
facts.quote: TheGamer: "These seats will be things like chairs, cages, or even toilets, and you unlock a trophy in Reanimal for sitting on ten in a playthrough."

facts.fact: Five lamb statues are hidden off the main path. Praying at one lights a candle in its hands, and you must find all five in one playthrough to earn the trophy.
facts.flag: Game Rant and TheGamer disagree on which mask the statues unlock, so the mask is left out.
facts.quote: TheGamer: "you can always pause to pray at five lamb statues hidden throughout several of the game's chapters." | TheGamer: "There are five statues hidden throughout the world in Reanimal that can be interacted with to light a candle in their hands for a moment of peace." | TheGamer: "You have to find all five hidden statues in a single playthrough to earn this trophy."

facts.fact: Reanimal has a secret ending. You must find all five hidden coffins in one playthrough, and opening each one releases a child's phantom.
facts.quote: Game Rant: "Opening these coffins will release a phantom of a child and a glimpse of the dreadful fate that befell them." | TheGamer: "You'll need to find all five coffins in one playthrough to get the secret ending in Reanimal"

facts.fact: Five Critters hide around the world, and killing each one gives you a unique mask.
facts.quote: Game Rant: "There are a total of five Critters that players can hunt down in REANIMAL, each giving players a unique mask to wear on their characters."

facts.fact: One Critter hides under a traffic cone, and killing it drops the Cone Head mask.
facts.quote: Game Rant: "Inside the room, you'll spot a traffic cone that has a spider-like creature underneath it." | Game Rant: "Players will receive the Cone Head mask by taking down the Critter in chapter two."

facts.fact: Hitting a scarecrow in a flower field knocks a Critter off it, and killing it gives the Deer Head mask.
facts.quote: Game Rant: "Approach the scarecrow and hit it with a melee weapon. A Critter will fall off the scarecrow, and you'll need to make quick work of it to get the Deer Head mask."

facts.fact: The boy fights with a crowbar and the girl with a knife.
facts.quote: Game Rant: "You'll need to use the Boy's Crowbar or the Girl's Knife to attack the critter until it's eliminated."

facts.fact: The boat is how you travel between areas, and steering it a total of 10,000 meters earns a trophy.
facts.quote: TheGamer: "While steering the boat you'll use to navigate between sections of the game, travel 10,000 meters in total."

facts.fact: Spiked naval mines float in the water. Once you have harpoons you can blow them up, and destroying 20 in one playthrough earns a trophy.
facts.quote: TheGamer: "As you sail around on your boat, you'll occasionally find naval mines floating in the water, large grayish-silver balls with spikes on the side. After accessing the harpoons, you can blow them up to clear them of their danger. Do so 20 times in one playthrough for this achievement."

facts.fact: Empty human skins lying around can suddenly come to life and slither after the children like snakes.
facts.quote: IGN: "the man/animal skins around us come to life, slithering after us like snakes."

facts.fact: Sniffer, the first enemy you must escape, is an impossibly tall man who skitters like a spider and bites your head off if he catches you.
facts.flag: Name from TheGamer, description from IGN.
facts.quote: TheGamer: "Sniffer, the very first enemy you'll need to escape" | IGN: "the first living human we encounter is impossibly tall, his face a Halloween mask of sagging skin, empty eye sockets, a maw that is always open. He skitters after us like a spider, biting our heads off if he catches us."

facts.fact: The tall figure can apparently travel through the bellies of bloated corpses, using them like fleshy portals.
facts.quote: GamesRadar: "who can also apparently use the bellies of bloated, distended corpses as some sort of fleshy, rib-lined portal to move around." | Push Square: "contorting monsters will appear and then disappear through dead bodies in the environment."

facts.fact: Sniffer has an ice cream van that turns on and chases the children down a hill, and its jingle can be heard in the distance.
facts.quote: TheGamer: "you'll see Sniffer's ice cream van from before, which turns on and begins to chase you down the hill." | PlayStation Blog: "A particular favourite of mine was the distant jingle of an ice cream van which foreshadowed"

facts.fact: Early on, the siblings fix up a pump trolley by finding its missing wheels, so they can ride it across the train tracks.
facts.quote: GamesRadar: "fix up a pump trolley to make it across train tracks." | PlayStation Blog: "ranging from simply finding wheels for a pump trolley"

facts.fact: Plunging a clogged toilet turns up a key, along with the deflated skin of what was once perhaps a man, his face caught between a person and a pig.
facts.quote: IGN: "A plunger applied to a clogged toilet reveals a key and the deformed, deflated skin of what was once, perhaps, a man; his features are off, deformed, his face caught between that of a person and a pig."

facts.fact: The island setting takes you through an abandoned factory, an unsettling forest, a sinkhole-plagued city and a waterlogged workshop, before opening up for freer exploration.
facts.quote: PlayStation Blog: "Your adventure across a fragmented island pushes you to an abandoned factory, an unsettling forest, a sinkhole-plagued city, and a waterlogged workshop, just for starters, before things vastly open up for more non-linear exploration."

facts.fact: The siblings are searching for three missing friends named Hood, Bucket and Bandage, each one held in a different area of the island.
facts.quote: PlayStation Blog: "they set off in their boat to find and reclaim their missing friends" | PlayStation Blog: "Hood, Bucket and Bandage" | GamesRadar: "as you travel these three main island areas - each one holding one of your friends"

facts.fact: A homicidal cloud of seagulls attacks the children at one point, which GamesRadar compared to The Birds.
facts.quote: GamesRadar: "Being attacked by a homicidal cloud of seagulls in full The Birds mode was a memorable event"

facts.fact: Obstacles in your way can be anything from a locked door to a giant, eyeless, crying whale.
facts.quote: GamesRadar: "With Reanimal that could be anything from a locked door to a giant eyeless crying whale, or worse."

facts.fact: Reanimal switched from the 2.5D platforming of Little Nightmares to a more fully 3D world, freeing the camera from what Tarsier calls the dollhouse view.
facts.quote: VGC: "there are clear differences here, most notably with the switch from 2.5D platforming to a more fully 3D environment." | Xbox Wire: "The camera was a big liberator this time around, because we weren't confined to that dollhouse camera."

facts.fact: Talking about the boat exploration, Tarsier's narrative director joked that The Legend of Zelda: The Wind Waker was an inspiration, though the tone is a complete 180 from it.
facts.quote: VGC: "Marvik joked that The Legend of Zelda: The Wind Waker was an inspiration – tonally, this is a complete 180 from that."
